management_guidance.text: Thanks, Tim, and good afternoon, everyone. Our March quarter revenue of $95.4 billion was up 5% year-over-year despite a headwind of almost 2.5 percentage points from foreign exchange. We also grew in the majority of the markets we track. Products revenue was $68.7 billion, up 3% year-over-year, driven by growth in iPhone, iPad, and Mac. And thanks to our high levels of customer satisfaction and strong loyalty, our installed base of active devices reached an all-time high across all product categories and geographic segments. Services revenue was $26.6 billion, up 12% year-over-year despite over 2 percentage points of foreign exchange headwinds. And as Tim mentioned, this was an all-time revenue record. We also grew in every geographic segment and saw double-digit growth in both developed and emerging markets. Company gross margin was 47.1%, in the middle of our guidance range and up 20 basis points sequentially primarily driven by favorable mix. Products gross margin was 35.9%, down 340 basis points sequentially, driven by mix, foreign exchange, and a seasonal loss of leverage. drivers.name: Tariff and trade-policy cost exposure

drivers.why_it_matters: Reported margin quality is flattered by a non-recurring ~2pp benefit, so the sustainable margin base is lower. Trade-policy shifts can swing Products gross margin by hundreds of basis points, directly moving EPS and the credibility of margin assumptions embedded in the multiple.

drivers.name: AI (Siri/Apple Intelligence) capability and upgrade pull
drivers.current_state: Next-generation Apple Intelligence powering Siri AI released September 14, 2026, positioned as a potential upgrade-cycle catalyst alongside the iPhone 18 Pro/A20 Pro launch; no adoption, usage, or review data available yet.
drivers.why_it_matters: AI differentiation is the main swing factor for upgrade pace across a 2.5B+ device base and for competitive position. Success lifts volumes, ASPs, and Services attach; failure leaves growth dependent on replacement timing alone, challenging the premium multiple.

drivers.name: iPhone upgrade cycle strength
drivers.current_state: Double-digit YoY iPhone revenue growth in both the March and June FY2026 quarters, setting records in both; iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max with the A20 Pro chip launched September 9, 2026; no early sell-through or pre-order data yet.
drivers.why_it_matters: iPhone is the largest revenue line and the entry point to the installed base that Services monetizes. Sustained double-digit cycle strength determines most of near-term enterprise value; a strong or weak iPhone 18/AI-driven cycle swings revenue, product mix, and the growth rate embedded in the premium multiple.

drivers.name: Installed base scale and engagement
drivers.current_state: Installed base of over 2.5 billion active devices, at an all-time high across all product categories and geographic segments, supported by high customer satisfaction and loyalty.
drivers.why_it_matters: The installed base is the compounding asset behind both revenue engines: it sets the ceiling on replacement hardware volume and the audience for high-margin Services. Its continued growth underwrites durable cash flows and terminal-value assumptions.

drivers.name: Services vs Products revenue mix
drivers.current_state: Services gross margin ~75.6–75.7% vs Products ~40.1%; company gross margin 50.06% in the June quarter. Near-term, June-quarter Products revenue grew 18% YoY vs Services 12%, temporarily leaning mix toward Products during the hardware cycle.
drivers.why_it_matters: With roughly a 35-point gross-margin gap between segments, each point of revenue mix shifted toward Services adds about a third of a point to company gross margin. This is the least cyclical margin lever and underpins terminal margin assumptions.

drivers.name: Geographic demand breadth (incl. Greater China)
drivers.current_state: Double-digit YoY growth in every geographic segment in the June FY2026 quarter, spanning developed and emerging markets; no regional revenue dollar figures are available in the pack.
drivers.why_it_matters: Broad geographic growth reduces concentration risk in any single region (notably Greater China) and signals genuine demand durability rather than channel or one-market effects. Regional policy or demand shocks would hit reported growth disproportionately.

drivers.name: iPhone and Mac supply constraints
drivers.current_state: Supply constraints on iPhone and, to a lesser extent, Mac cited in the March FY2026 quarter and still present into the June quarter, which nonetheless delivered double-digit growth in every geographic segment; magnitude and duration unquantified.
drivers.why_it_matters: Near-term, unmet demand defers rather than destroys revenue, but constraints persisting into the iPhone 18 ramp could cap launch-quarter volume, distort product mix, and delay the AI-driven upgrade cycle the market is pricing.

core_claims.title: Sustainable gross margin sits below the reported June-quarter level
core_claims.statement: Apple's fiscal 2026 third quarter (ended June 27, 2026) set June-quarter records for total company revenue, EPS, iPhone, Mac, and Services revenue, per the company's SEC-filed press release. The reported gross margin for the quarter, any one-time tariff-refund benefit, and the sustainable margin base relative to the reported level are not disclosed in the available evidence and remain unverified
core_claims.why_it_matters: Margin assumptions embedded in the premium multiple rest on the reported level. If the true run-rate is lower, both EPS and the multiple face downward pressure, and the margin narrative shifts from structural improvement to a policy windfall.

core_claims.title: iPhone double-digit growth is a durable reacceleration, not a cycle peak
core_claims.statement: iPhone revenue set new March quarter and June quarter records in fiscal 2026, per Apple's Q2 and Q3 FY2026 earnings releases (primary, tier-1 sources); the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max were announced September 9, 2026, and next-generation Siri AI shipped September 14, 2026. The year-over-year iPhone growth rate in either quarter is not quantified in the available evidence, and whether growth persists through the iPhone 18 cycle or marks a peak before replacement demand normalizes remains an open question with neither supporting nor opposing evidence in the set
core_claims.why_it_matters: iPhone is the largest revenue line and the funnel into the installed base that Services monetizes. The premium multiple assumes growth persistence, so the gap between durable reacceleration and a two-quarter spike is the biggest single revenue swing factor.

core_claims.title: Siri AI is the upgrade-cycle accelerant the market is paying for
core_claims.statement: Apple released the next generation of Apple Intelligence powering Siri AI on September 14, 2026, five days after the September 9, 2026 announcement of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max (both confirmed by primary Apple sources; the on-sale date of the hardware is not in evidence). No adoption, usage, review, upgrade-intent, trade-in, or sell-through data exists in the evidence set, so any demand or upgrade-cycle acceleration effect from Siri AI is unverified. The assertions that Siri AI is 'positioned as the catalyst' for upgrades or that 'the market is paying for' it are unsupported by…
core_claims.why_it_matters: AI differentiation is the main swing factor for upgrade pace and competitive position across a base of more than 2.5 billion active devices. Success lifts volumes, ASPs, and Services attach; failure leaves growth dependent on replacement timing alone, a path the premium multiple cannot support.

core_claims.title: Total return depends on expectations, not just results
core_claims.statement: Apple's fiscal 2026 third quarter (ended June 27, 2026) set June-quarter records for total company revenue and EPS, per the company's primary 8-K exhibit. The broader assertion — that at a premium trailing earnings multiple total return hinges on growth and margin assumptions holding, and that a post-earnings one-day decline on elevated volume after a quarter that beat expectations demonstrated multiple compression dominating operating outcomes — is not established by the evidence in this set, which contains no price, volume, valuation-multiple, or consensus-estimate data
core_claims.why_it_matters: The market is paying for continuation of double-digit growth and roughly fifty percent gross margins. Any deceleration or margin-quality miss, such as the tariff benefit not repeating, compresses the multiple faster than fundamentals deteriorate, so expectations risk dominates total-return scenarios.

core_claims.title: Services mix is the structural margin floor beneath a cyclical hardware cycle
core_claims.statement: Apple's Products (iPhone, Mac) and Services segments both set June-quarter revenue records in fiscal Q3 2026, and Services revenue reached an all-time high in fiscal Q2 2026, alongside records for total company revenue and EPS in both quarters; a hardware refresh cycle is active (iPhone 18 Pro launched September 2026). The relative gross margin profiles of the two segments, their relative growth rates, and the resulting revenue-mix and company gross margin trajectory are not established in the current evidence set
core_claims.why_it_matters: Terminal margin assumptions rest on the structural Services mix trend. If the hardware cycle keeps leaning mix toward Products, reported margin gains stall even as revenue grows, weakening the margin narrative that supports the multiple.

pm_synthesis.what_matters_now: Two questions dominate: does the iPhone 18 / Siri AI launch window (2026-09-09 and 2026-09-14) extend the double-digit growth run, and does the ~37.9x TTM multiple survive the roll-off of the ~2pp tariff-refund margin benefit in the June quarter (rev_f680a2738ac040b7a37c1e15345b143a)? Evidence coverage is poor on both: no sell-through, adoption, consensus, forward-multiple, or FCF data in the set, and three of five core claims are unverified.
what_changed: Q3 FY2026 (reported 2026-07-30): revenue $109.4B, +16% YoY; EPS $2.02, +29% YoY; gross margin 50.1% including ~2pp favorable tariff-refund impact and $0.11 of EPS (rev_f680a2738ac040b7a37c1e15345b143a).
iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max announced 2026-09-09 (rev_9685524991084f70bc6b15246e0d4aad); next-generation Siri AI shipped 2026-09-14 (rev_a813d9313b8f4332a30429331fd2a01e).

Validation pass downgraded the margin-quality, market-reaction, and Services-mix claims to unverified (bclm_aaff24b577fc43db8cf909715a0cb353, bclm_206dcfe484184314a710333afcf22562, bclm_50cb5246e283434c80d438a586cb8495).
All scenario events in the set are flagged scenario_only with no base-case change and no affected claims.

pm_synthesis.strongest_support: Two consecutive primary-source record quarters: Q3 FY2026 revenue $109.4B (+16% YoY), EPS $2.02 (+29% YoY), June-quarter records for total revenue, EPS, iPhone, Mac, and Services (rev_f680a2738ac040b7a37c1e15345b143a); Q2 FY2026 revenue $111.2B (+17% YoY), EPS $2.01 (+22% YoY), Services all-time high, double-digit growth in every geographic segment (rev_f380aa032a3041bea9ca174726be3187). Both launches are confirmed by primary Apple sources (rev_9685524991084f70bc6b15246e0d4aad, rev_a813d9313b8f4332a30429331fd2a01e).
pm_synthesis.strongest_counter: Claim-level evidence is thin exactly where it matters: no data on iPhone 18 pre-orders or sell-through, Siri AI adoption, the sustainable margin base ex-tariff-refund, or consensus. The market-reaction claim (bclm_206dcfe484184314a710333afcf22562) lists the -7.35% one-day drop on 2.6x volume as unsupported; those figures appear only in validated state bst_8e89fcabdfd749708c158d332f4c9101 with no bound price/volume evidence. Counter-searches found no opposing evidence, so the bear case is untested, not refuted.

base_bull_bear.base: Record March and June quarters plus a normal iPhone 18 launch keep growth positive, but the ~2pp tariff-refund margin benefit rolls off and the FX tailwind can fade (state bst_11580c42f2664b5eb2dcc7db5a5fb4af); at ~37.9x TTM (header), earnings growth is largely offset by multiple risk. Sideways stock.
